titleStmt.title: Kephalaia of the Teacher, edition page 90: diplomatic and Leiden transcription

sourceDesc.bibl: Kephalaia (Manichäische Handschriften der Staatlichen Museen Berlin), ed. H. J. Polotsky and A. Böhlig, Stuttgart: Kohlhammer, 90. Restorations, sublinear dots, gap counts and corrections are the editors'.

encodingDesc.p: EpiDoc. Read by eye from the page image; gap counts, sublinear dots and supralinear stroke extents verified by measurement on the image. A supralinear stroke is marked on every letter it covers by at least half its width. Spaces are the edition's word division. Facsimile zones are measured line centres. The editors' German statements are not transcribed: each is mapped to an id of the controlled vocabulary data/kephalaia/editorial_vocabulary.json and carried as @ana (ed: statements in the text, app: apparatus footnotes, tr: categories of the transcriber's commentary).

app.note: "In ϯⲟⲩⲱϣⲉ steht ⲱ über der Linie": the ⲱ is written above the line; the place is named, so it is encoded `\ⲱ/` (48.20).
"Von ⲡⲁϫⲉ nur ganz unsichere Spuren": the letters of ⲡⲁϫⲉ rest on very uncertain traces.
"Hinter ⲁϫⲱⲩ klein über der Zeile: ⲉⲩⲟ ⲙ̄ⲙⲏⲉ ⲛⲁϩⲣⲉⲕ": words written small above the line after ⲁϫⲱⲩ, not printed in the line (the same words stand in ll. 16–17); text unchanged (82.25).
"Anfang ⲧⲉ ⲧϩⲁⲗⲙⲉ nur unsichere Spuren": the beginning of the line rests on uncertain traces.
"Erg. viell. ϫⲛ̄ ⲛ̄ⲧⲉϥ[ϩⲗⲡⲉ], also Dittogr.": the editors suggest restoring [ϩⲗⲡⲉ] in the bracket, i.e. a dittography of ϫⲛ̄ ⲛⲧⲉϥϩⲗⲡⲉ earlier in the line; nothing changed in the text.
